Such negative energy fluxes seeming\u00adly lead to a breakdown of the second law of thermodynamics. It is argued that such a breakdown will not in fact occur if a negative energy flux F is constrained by an inequality of the form \u2502F\u2502\u2272 T-2 where T is a character\u00adistic time over which the negative energy flux occurs. Particular models in which negative energy fluxes occur are examined, and it is found that such an inequality is indeed satisfied. Quantum violations of the dominant energy condition, which requires that the local energy density be greater than or equal to the magnitude of the pressure are also discussed briefly.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1098\/rspa.1978.0197","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2006,12,18]],"date-time":"2006-12-18T17:49:02Z","timestamp":1166464142000},"page":"227-236","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":141,"title":["Quantum coherence effects and the second law of thermodynamics"],"prefix":"10.1098","volume":"364","author":[{"given":"L.
